cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, and his brother Aaron (Exodus 4:14) have a message from the LORD, and the people of Israel believed it (Exodus 4:31). Now they take it straight to Pharaoh, king of Egypt. Friend, I used to hold my breath every time somebody opened the junk drawer I lived in, and these two walk right up to a KING.

cards.question: Moses and Aaron bring Pharaoh a message from the LORD, the God of Israel. Why does the LORD want Pharaoh to let His people go?

answers.text: To hold a feast to Him in the wilderness
To go back to their own land for good
To rest from their labor for a season

cards.text: Pharaoh listens to the whole message. Then he fires right back with a question of his own.

cards.question: What does Pharaoh ask Moses and Aaron?

answers.text: Who is the LORD that I should obey Him
Where will your people go after the feast
How many of your people want to leave

cards.text: Pharaoh says he doesn't know the LORD, and he will not let Israel go. Moses and Aaron answer that the God of the Hebrews has met with them, and this time they add a please: “Please let us go on a three-day journey into the wilderness to sacrifice to the LORD our God…”

cards.question: Moses and Aaron warn Pharaoh that if they don't go, the LORD may strike them with plagues or with the sword.

cards.text: Pharaoh wants to know why Moses and Aaron are drawing the people away from their work. Then he snaps, “Get back to your labor!”

cards.question: Pharaoh also tells Moses and Aaron that the people of the land are now numerous. What's his point?

answers.text: Moses and Aaron would stop a lot of workers
There are too many people to travel that far
They could grow strong enough to fight Egypt

cards.text: That same day, Pharaoh gives orders to the taskmasters of the people and their foremen. I bet he's not just mad, he's SAME-DAY mad.

cards.question: Pharaoh orders that the people will no longer be supplied with ___ for making bricks.

cards.text: From now on, they have to go gather their own straw. That's like telling me to go out and hunt down my own chocolate chips before every single batch.

cards.question: Since the people now have to gather their own straw, Pharaoh tells the taskmasters to lower the brick quota.
Pharaoh tells the taskmasters the people keep crying out to go and sacrifice to their God because they are ___.
Pharaoh orders the work made harder so the men will be kept busy and pay no attention to what he calls lies.

cards.text: The taskmasters and foremen go out with Pharaoh's message: no more straw, get your own wherever you can find it, and your workload won't be reduced at all.

cards.question: The people have to find their own straw now. Where do they go to gather stubble for straw?

answers.text: All over the land of Egypt
Only to the fields of Goshen

cards.text: And the taskmasters keep pressing them: “Fulfill your quota each day, just as you did when straw was provided.”
Then the Israelite foremen, the ones Pharaoh's taskmasters set over the people, are beaten.

cards.question: The Israelite foremen are asked why they haven't fulfilled their brick quota yesterday or today, as they did before.

cards.text: The Israelite foremen go straight to Pharaoh: “Why are you treating your servants this way?” No straw, they say, and yet they're still told to make bricks.

cards.question: The foremen tell Pharaoh his servants are being beaten, but the fault is with his own ___.

cards.text: “You are slackers!” Pharaoh replies, and then again, “Slackers!” That's why, he says, they keep saying, “Let us go and sacrifice to the LORD.”

cards.question: Pharaoh tells the foremen they'll get straw again, as long as they still deliver the full quota of bricks.

cards.text: The foremen realize they're in trouble when they hear the daily quota isn't going down. When they leave Pharaoh, Moses and Aaron are standing there waiting to meet them.

cards.question: What do the foremen say to Moses and Aaron?

answers.text: May the LORD look on you and judge you
May the LORD bless you for your courage
May the LORD go with you to Pharaoh

cards.text: They say Moses and Aaron have made them a stench before Pharaoh and his officials. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer under dust and old takeout menus, and NOBODY ever called me a stench.

cards.question: The foremen tell Moses and Aaron they've put a sword in the hand of Pharaoh and his officials to kill the foremen.

cards.text: So Moses goes back to the LORD. And he doesn't hold one thing back.

cards.question: Moses comes before the LORD with a question. What does he ask?

answers.text: Why have You brought trouble upon this people
Who will You send to Pharaoh instead of me
How long must Your people wait in Egypt

cards.question: Moses also asks the LORD whether this is why He sent him.
Moses says that ever since he spoke to Pharaoh in the LORD's name, Pharaoh has brought trouble on the people, and the LORD has not ___ His people in any way.

cards.text: Moses brought the hard question. Now the LORD answers him.

cards.question: What does the LORD tell Moses he will now see?

answers.text: What the LORD will do to Pharaoh
A new leader rise up in Egypt

cards.question: The LORD says that because of His mighty hand, Pharaoh will let the people go. And because of His strong hand, what will Pharaoh do with them?

answers.text: Drive them out of his land

cards.text: We'll let the dough rest right there, friend. This story still has plenty left in the oven.
